title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
The failure here is impersonation: scammers used AI-generated video and fabricated social media profiles to present a real, named attorney as the source of fraudulent legal services. The deception happened entirely outside any system the attorney controlled, on third-party social media platforms, and it required the victim to have no independent way to verify that the face and name in a video corresponded to the actual person. The mechanism that made it effective was the combination of a convincing likeness, a plausible service, and payment channels that are difficult to reverse.

The deployment context is social media distribution rather than a single platform or product, which meant the fraud replicated across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram simultaneously and at scale. Detection depended on victims calling the real attorney's office, not on any automated platform check, and remediation required hiring a specialist anti-piracy firm. Nearly 6,500 profiles were removed before the scheme was reported, suggesting the platforms' own moderation did not catch it proactively.

What is not established is who created the AI-generated content, where the operation originated, or whether any platform bears legal responsibility, as these questions were still being referred to authorities at the time of reporting.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience has become a victim of artificial intelligence fraud targeting vulnerable immigrants. Angel Leal discovered that scammers created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos using his likeness to promote fraudulent immigration services. The videos falsely advertise services such as US residency assistance for undocumented immigrants in exchange for cash payments of around $2,200. Leal first learned of the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, and the situation has escalated significantly over the past three months.

To combat the fraud, Leal's office hired an anti-piracy company that successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically direct victims through social media videos to WhatsApp numbers, where fraudsters exchange fake contracts and request payments via Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal warns immigrants to verify identities before paying for legal services and notes his office never requests payments over the phone. He plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the source of these scams.
